86.line: | 86 | 🟢 (filed 🟡) **The `/clean_gone` repair lives only in GITIGNORED vendored plugin files, so the next `/plugin update` silently un-fixes it — and the directory it sits in is a git checkout, which makes the wrong answer look verified** — filed 2026-09-02 at the user's request, by the session that made the repair. ⛔ **MEASURED, and "vendored" understates the trap.** Two byte-identical copies exist (`diff` reports no difference): `~/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/claude-plugins-official/plugins/commit-commands/commands/clean_gone.md` and `~/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/commit-commands/d45efab8c85b/commands/clean_gone.md`. The marketplace one sits inside a **real git checkout** whose `origin` is `kujinlee/claude-config`, so `git status` there runs, succeeds, and looks authoritative — **but `.gitignore` line 3 is a bare `*`**, and `git check-ignore -v` on the file returns `.gitignore:3:*`. `git status --untracked-files=all` over that subtree is **EMPTY**: the file cannot even surface as a `??`. **Anyone who checks "is the fix committed?" by running `git status` in that directory receives a clean tree that means nothing at all** — this is the *green check over the wrong subject* shape, arriving for free from a tool nobody suspects. ⚠ **HOW THE UPDATE ACTUALLY LOSES IT, since "reverts" is imprecise:** `installed_plugins.json` records `gitCommitSha: d45efab8c85b3fee…` and the cache path's version segment IS that SHA, so an update does not overwrite the edited file — it installs a **new** directory keyed by a **new** SHA and stops reading the old one. Nothing is modified, nothing warns, and the edit is simply orphaned in a directory that has become invisible. A destructive overwrite would at least be detectable; this is quieter. ⚠ **WHAT WOULD BE LOST — four repairs, each paid for by a measured failure**, all quoted from the current file: (1) `git fetch --prune` as step 1, with the fixture recorded inline — *"BEFORE prune, git branch -v [gone] count: 0 / AFTER prune, … count: 2"*; (2) the warning that `git branch -v` prints the literal `[gone]` while `-vv` prints `[origin/<branch>: gone]` instead, so the grep matches nothing (verified on git 2.49.0); (3) a skip for the branch you are standing on, whose comment records the measured death — *"the loop dies on 'cannot delete branch used by worktree'"*; (4) echoing each SHA before `git branch -D` so a force-deleted branch leaves a reflog handle in the transcript. ⛔ **THE FAILURE SIGNATURE IF IT REVERTS IS A FALSE GREEN, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS 🟡 AND NOT 🟢:** without the prune, `/clean_gone` reports *"no cleanup was needed"* on a repository full of stale branches. The file says so in its own words — *"Skipping this step does not produce an error — it produces a confident 'no cleanup was needed' on a repository full of branches that need cleaning."* This project's own rule is that a check which cannot reach what it measures must fail loudly, and a reverted `/clean_gone` fails silently in the direction of "all clear". **SHAPE:** add a repo-tracked `.claude/commands/clean_gone.md` carrying the repaired procedure, exactly as `docs/plugins.md` already prescribes for `mattpocock:handoff` — layer 3 (a vendored edit) is a convenience, never a mechanism, and `git` restoring the file IS the mechanism. `.claude/commands/` already exists in this repo with one member (`session-skills.md`), so this adds a file, not a pattern. ⚠ **CHECK THIS FIRST, BECAUSE IT DECIDES THE SHAPE AND IT IS NOT YET CONFIRMED:** a repo command appears to invoke as `/clean_gone` while the plugin's is listed as `/commit-commands:clean_gone`, which means the two **COEXIST under different names** — the repo copy would NOT override the plugin one, and anyone typing the plugin's name after an update still gets the unrepaired version. **FALSIFIER:** create the repo command, run `/plugin update`, then invoke the plugin's name and check whether step 1 is `git fetch --prune`. If it is not, a second layer is needed — either the plugin name must be shadowed, or the repo command's description must say plainly that it supersedes the plugin's. ⚠ **DO NOT re-patch the vendored files as the fix.** That is what this row exists to stop; doing it again would reset the clock without changing anything. ⟦kind: defect⟧ | `.claude/commands/clean_gone.md` (new), `docs/plugins.md` (a pointer row alongside the existing `mattpocock:handoff` three-layer table) | XS | (tooling) | **FIX OPEN IN PR #210 — filed and fixed the same day, 2026-09-02.** The durable copy ships as `.claude/commands/clean_gone.md` with a four-line rule in `docs/plugins.md`. ⚠ **NOT fully closed, and the residue is the part that decides whether one layer is enough:** the precedence falsifier is UNRUN — a repo command appears to invoke as `/clean_gone` while the plugin's is `/commit-commands:clean_gone`, so the two may COEXIST rather than one shadowing the other, leaving the plugin's name serving the unrepaired version after an update. Running it mutates the local plugin install, so it waits for the user. 🟡 not 🟢: nothing is broken today, but the protection was held by the weakest of the three layers `docs/plugins.md` names, and its reversion produces a confident false "no cleanup needed" rather than an error. Not 🟠: no money, no correctness path, and the blast radius is one maintenance command. ⟳ re-rated 2026-10-24: 🟡 → 🟢 — the durable copy shipped (`b3d44f09`, PR #210); the residue is one falsifier run. ⟳ 2026-10-24: PARTLY — the durable copy shipped (`b3d44f09`, PR #210; `.claude/commands/clean_gone.md`). Remains: the precedence falsifier, which mutates the local plugin install and so waits for the user. ⟳ audited 2026-10-26: NEEDS-OWNER-ACTION — still waiting on the user to run the `/plugin update` precedence falsifier, which mutates the local install. |

198.line: | 198 | 🟠 **`CONTEXT.md` has NO vocabulary for the recall subsystem - and this is the THIRD time one architecture review has prescribed the same repair for the same symptom** - filed 2026-09-30 by the Phase 6 architecture review (F3, docs/reviews/architecture-review-2026-09-30-recall-matcher.md). ⛔ **MEASURED over `CONTEXT.md`, substring-checked:** `recall` **0**, `arm` **0**, `fire` **0**, `plan verdict` **0**, `rubric` **0**, `situation` **0**, `memory entry` **0**. ⚠ The substring check is the reason to trust the zeros - a naive `grep -ic arm` returns **1**, whose only hit is inside the word *harmless*; the `cache` (10), `trigger` (2) and `corpus` (1) hits all belong to the mutation harness or to that file's own self-description. ⭐⭐ **THE PATTERN, with three data points and one prescribed repair every time:** (1) **Architecture Review #7, 2026-09-03** added the whole *Verification Stack (Repo Tooling)* section, recording that *"seven consecutive review rounds had been argued in words this file did not contain: with no shared terms, each round could only name the instance in front of it, and the same defect kept recurring in a sibling"*; (2) **the review-verdict path, 2026-09-23** added *Testimony* and *Review identity*, recording *"the component had been argued for four rounds in vocabulary the glossary did not contain, which is the same failure Architecture Review #7 recorded"*; (3) **this fold** - two rounds, four reviewers, the same defect recurring in a sibling six times, and zero shared terms. **The diagnosis has been identical three times, which makes the absence of a trigger the finding.** ⚠ **The terms are not yet named, deliberately** - naming them is the grilling half of `improve-codebase-architecture` and belongs in a conversation, not in this row. Candidates the subsystem argues in daily and the glossary cannot express: the *situation* (a step's Doing line, the unit matched against), the *trigger* (`FIRES-WHEN:`, the unit matched FROM), *arm* vs *fire* (one model call vs a cache lookup), the *plan verdict*, and *already-embodied* (the rubric boundary measured as the binding variable). **FALSIFIER:** this row is wrong if the subsystem can be argued about in terms `CONTEXT.md` already defines - the three prior rounds' documents are the corpus to test that against. ⟦kind: task⟧ | `CONTEXT.md` | S | (process / deliverable #2) | 🟠 **OPEN - filed 2026-09-30 by the architecture review.** ⭐ Third instance of one repair. ⛔ Do NOT invent terms from the code's identifiers - take them from the words the three review rounds actually used and could not define. ⟳ audited 2026-10-26: NEEDS-OWNER — still no recall vocabulary in CONTEXT.md; the row assigns term-naming to a grilling conversation, so it waits on the owner. |

306.line: | 306 | 🟠 **THE DECISION PROCEDURE'S INPUT WAS NEVER WRITTEN — 0 OF 15 OF A BRANCH'S ROUND DOCUMENTS CARRY THE HEADER THEIR OWN TEMPLATE CALLS MANDATORY, AND THE ONE SCRIPT THAT ANSWERS *IS THIS THRASHING?* EXITS CANNOT RUN (rc=2) ON THAT SUBJECT** — found 2026-10-19 by the Phase 6 review's Claude half (H5), which **refuted the coordinator's claim that this was a witnessed instance of backlog #184** and is right. ⛔ **IT IS NEITHER backlog #184 NOR backlog #136, and the distinction decides the remedy.** backlog #184 is about DISCOVERY (*nothing brings the card to the moment it is needed*) and its work item is *build a caller* — a caller on this branch returns **rc=2**, so backlog #184's fix does not reach this. backlog #136 is about the RUBRIC for continue-vs-stop; the rubric exists, is written in three places, and simply was not consultable. **This row is about the INPUT.** ⭐ **MEASURED:** `docs/round-header-template.md:3` — *"Every **coordinator** round document carries this block immediately after its title"* — and its stated purpose (`:5-8`) is this decision and no other: *"The decision procedure needs two counters — consecutive fix-induced rounds and rounds since a finding in the deliverable. On PR #302 nobody kept either, **which is why four rounds ran where two were owed**."* Counts: this branch's round documents with a ```yaml header **0 of 15**; round documents elsewhere under `docs/reviews/` with one **77**. `python3 scripts/check-review-decision.py` → *"CANNOT RUN — a round document for 'chrome-bar-reachable' has no usable header: no ```yaml header block"*, **rc=2**. Its own suite is healthy (**61/61**), so this is not a broken guard — it is a guard whose subject was never written, across **8 rounds and 3 writers**, while 77 siblings comply. A `grep -ril` for the card across that branch's 15 round documents returns **nothing**. ⛔ **THE CAUSAL CHAIN, and it is the one the repo already paid for once:** the counters were never recorded → the only instrument that reads them cannot run → the arming call had to be made from recall → it was, five times, and was attributed to an authority that does not exist (see the amended rows 184 and 136, and the review's F2). The template was bought with PR #302's *"four rounds ran where two were owed"*; this branch skipped it in every document and the failure recurred as **five rounds where zero were owed**. ⭐ **CHEAPEST FIX, AND IT IS NOT A NEW MECHANISM:** backfill the header on the three coordinator notes (r3, r5, r6) from evidence already inside them — their per-round fix-induced tables ARE the counters — then run `check-review-decision.py` and record its answer in the round document. Minutes of work, and it is the single action that would have prevented the Phase 6 review that found it. **FALSIFIER:** a count of round documents lacking the ```yaml header, currently **0 of 15** compliant on this subject against **77** compliant elsewhere; it goes green when that count is 15 of 15 and `check-review-decision.py` returns an answer rather than rc=2. ⚠ A cannot-run recorded as a pass is this project's strongest available false claim (`CONTEXT.md`'s *Cannot-run*), so **do not let a future round read rc=2 as "no thrashing"**. ⟦kind: defect⟧ | `docs/round-header-template.md`, `docs/reviews/coordinator/chrome-bar-reachable-r{3,5,6}-coordinator.md`, `scripts/check-review-decision.py` (consumer, unchanged) | S | (process) | 🟠 **PARTLY CLOSED 2026-10-24 — THE BACKFILL IS DONE AND THE INSTRUMENT STILL SAYS CANNOT RUN, for a different and truer reason.** The three coordinator notes (r3, r5, r6) now carry headers, every field DERIVED from the round's halves, the notes' own fix-induced tables and the fold commits, with a provenance section in each naming its source; `rounds_for('chrome-bar-reachable')` parses all three (6 + 8 + 9 findings). ⛔ **`decide` → CANNOT_RUN, rc=2: *rounds are not gapless: found [3, 5, 6]*.** The procedure reads coordinator documents only and this branch wrote them for 3 of its 8 rounds. ⚠ **The FALSIFIER as written cannot go green:** *15 of 15* counts the 12 halves, which `round-header-template.md` says structurally cannot carry `disposition`/`fixes_nontrivial` — the right count is coordinator documents, now **3 of 3**. Reaching an answer needs a DECISION, not a backfill: author coordinator documents for r1, r2, r4, r7, r8 with hindsight (the circularity backlog #318 and backlog #314 caution against), or change what `sequence_error` asks of a subject whose coordinator notes are sparse. Recorded in the r6 note, with the warning that this rc=2 is not "no thrashing". Sibling of backlog #184 and backlog #136 and blocked by neither. ⟳ audited 2026-10-26: NEEDS-OWNER — the backfill is done; the CANNOT_RUN stays until the owner picks between back-authoring the r1/r2/r4/r7/r8 coordinator documents and changing what `sequence_error` requires. ⟳ 2026-10-28: this one STAYS the owner's, deliberately — the only option this row does not caution against, changing what `sequence_error` requires of a subject whose coordinator notes are sparse, loosens the decision procedure's input contract, which is CRITICAL under the owner's standing rule. ⟳ DECIDED 2026-10-29 by the owner (selection card): BACK-AUTHOR the missing headers for the five round documents, marked retroactive; `sequence_error` is not relaxed. |

307.line: | 307 | 🟡 (filed 🟠) **`MEMORY.md` HOLDS A SECOND, INDEPENDENT COPY OF THE MATCHING SIGNAL THAT THE MATCHER NEVER READS — AND THE COPY HAS ALREADY DRIFTED, AT A MEASURED COST TO THE OWNER** — found 2026-10-19 by the baseline survey (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-19-memory-recall-survey.md` §5) while answering the owner's question about compacting the index. ⭐ **MEASURED: 145 index rows carry a prose hook; 158 corpus files carry a `FIRES-WHEN:` trigger.** `scripts/recall-llm.py:431-432` excludes the index BY NAME — *"MEMORY.md is the INDEX, not an entry"* — so since the matcher shipped 2026-09-30 the two signals have had **one reader each**: the index is the ALWAYS-LOADED surface, the triggers are the MATCHED surface, and nothing reconciles them. ⛔ **THE DRIFT IS NOT HYPOTHETICAL AND THE OWNER CAUGHT IT:** the index row for `the-user-does-not-follow-in-real-time` described the step banner as `## ▶ STEP n of N`, while the file it points at has carried `[mm-dd hh:mm]` prepended since 2026-10-16 under a heading reading *"take it from here and do not re-derive it"*. **The assistant copied the ROW, not the FILE**, dropped timestamps entirely, and on being corrected re-derived a THIRD format (`▶ 13:25 PDT ·` — timezone, no date, `·` separator, all three explicitly forbidden) and wrote that into the durable spec. **A stale always-loaded copy beat a correct matched one**, which is this repo's most-measured failure class (`check-vocabulary-collisions`, 17 instances) reproduced in the memory subsystem. ⚠ **THE INDEX IS ALSO OVER ITS READ LIMIT, which is how the question arose rather than being the defect: 27.8 KB against 24.4 KB, so the last 2.8 KB — 30 pointer rows — is silently dropped on EVERY load.** ⭐ **But NOTHING is currently unreachable, measured: 0 entries.** All 30 dropped rows point at files carrying a trigger, so the matcher still reaches them; 4 files lack a trigger and all 4 sit inside the loaded region. **The two paths cover each other BY LUCK, NOT BY DESIGN**, and the exposure is precise — a future entry whose row lands past the limit AND whose description carries no trigger clause. ⛔ **TRIMMING PROSE CANNOT FIX THE SIZE — the row COUNT is binding, measured:** capping every hook at 70 chars still lands at 21,587 bytes against a 17,100 target, and showing the slug instead of the title makes it **BIGGER** (+427, slugs average 33 chars against titles' 30). Hooks only for an always-on tier (cap 110) reaches **14,933** with ~25 entries of headroom; a pure table of contents reaches 12,544. ⚠ **No guard parses this file** (`check-memory-link.py` counts FILES, `recall-llm.py` excludes it), so the format is unconstrained — which means the constraint is semantic, not mechanical. ⭐ **ON THE OWNER'S ACTUAL QUESTION — symbols or prose?** The status glyphs (`⭐ ⛔ ✅ ⟳`) are read as FLAGS, not matched, and compress freely. **A symbol standing in for a SITUATION reintroduces the arm measured dead** — token overlap scored **3/20** with **11.7%** false fires, and an abbreviation must be decoded before it can be matched. The 610 digit characters in the index are evidence that cannot be acted on without opening the file, and compress best by DELETION. **FALSIFIER:** an index hook and its file's `FIRES-WHEN:` trigger state different rules for the same fact — currently **at least 1** (the banner format, fixed 2026-10-19), with 145 rows unaudited. ⛔ **A guard here is premature:** the right remedy may be to stop the index carrying hooks at all, which would delete the surface rather than check it. ⟦kind: defect⟧ | the assistant's project memory index (outside this repo, hardlinked to `docs/memory/`), `scripts/recall-llm.py` (consumer, unchanged) | S–M + design | (process / deliverable #2) | 🟠 **PARTLY CLOSED 2026-10-19 — THE OVERFLOW IS FIXED, THE KEYING QUESTION IS UNTOUCHED, and keeping those apart is the point.** ⟳ The owner approved ONE specific move on a selection card this session — cut the 28 **slice-history** rows to `docs/memory/slice-history.md` as a TRIGGERED corpus entry. Index **26,930 → 22,078 CHARACTERS**, under the 24,985-character limit by 2,907, so nothing is dropped ⟳ (the unit is r1 CLAUDE H1's correction — the harness counts characters, and this row first said bytes) and the measured *"30 pointer rows silently discarded on EVERY load"* is no longer true. ⭐ That is exactly the remedy this row measured as the only one that works — *"TRIMMING PROSE CANNOT FIX THE SIZE, the row COUNT is binding"* — and it needed no answer to the hook question, because removing a whole SECTION is not compacting hooks. ⛔ **THE PROHIBITION BELOW STILL STANDS FOR WHAT IT WAS ABOUT.** The owner's *"work with me together when I get back to desk"* was about whether the index keeps prose hooks AT ALL — 145 rows, the always-loaded-vs-matched surface, backlog #191's keying question. **Not one hook was touched, re-worded or dropped.** That half is unchanged and still theirs. ⟳ Newly mechanical: `scripts/check-memory-index-budget.py` fails over budget and warns at 90%, so the size half cannot silently return — this row said *"no guard parses this file"* and that sentence is now false for SIZE and still true for the hook surface. ⛔ **AND MY CORRECTION OF THE ROW'S *"4 files lack a trigger"* WAS ITSELF WRONG — r1 CODEX finding #3 caught it and I reproduced it.** I measured `frontmatter_description` and reported **2 of 163**; the matcher needs a PARSED trigger, not merely a description. Re-measured through `memory_files` + `frontmatter_description` + `parse_trigger`: **163 files, 161 with a description, 159 with a parsed trigger, 4 WITHOUT** — so this row's original 4 was right all along. The two I missed carry a description whose trigger does not parse: `cannot-die-may-mean-a-second-clause` and `the-apparatus-outgrew-its-subject`. ⚠ **Measuring the wrong predicate is this row's OWN defect class reproduced while editing it** — `measure-the-population-the-code-actually-sees`, and the predicate that matters is the one the consumer applies. Original note, kept verbatim because it still governs the open half: (*"Let's be a little careful … work with me together when I get back to desk"*). Blocked on the same keying question as backlog #191, because whether the index keeps hooks depends on whether the matcher is trusted as the sole matching path — and the survey measured it returning `NONE` on 71% of steps. ⟳ re-rated 2026-10-24: 🟠 → 🟡 — the money/data-loss half (index rows silently dropped) is closed. ⟳ 2026-10-24: PARTLY — the overflow half is fixed (`slice-history.md`, `check-memory-index-budget.py`). Remains: the keying question. ⟳ audited 2026-10-26: NEEDS-OWNER — the size half is fixed; the hook-keying half still waits on the owner ('work with me together when I get back to desk'). |

MEASURED on master `f0dfef07`: the suite's open work is **31 rows (🟠6 🟡19 🟢6)** across three feature nodes, and it has **five names in four vocabularies** (a backlog tag, three anchors, three feature nodes, "goal 1", "D2" — the tag-vocabulary survey, `docs/explainers/2026-10-27-topic-tag-vocabulary-survey.html`). Both are now answered as part of this design; both rows are closed. ⟳ NEEDS-OWNER — the owner's walkthrough of the roles review page (several answers open). ⟳ 2026-10-28 (PR #434 round 1, C3, recorded not fixed): the dashboard's "What needs you" still lists every open PR (`gen-dashboard.open_prs()`), which the goal tree also shows, placed in its threads — a second, structureless answer to *what is in flight*.
